guide: Start here: open Start and type the household name, the two partner names, the extra payment a month and the date of the next payday in the yellow cells.
Replace demo data, step 1: clear the demo rows of Debts and type your own debts with balance, yearly rate, minimum payment and due day; keep the header row and leave paid-off debts at balance zero.
Replace demo data, step 2: clear Debt payments, Income and Net worth and paste your own rows; the schedules, the orders and the ratios fill in by themselves.
Pay-day routine: pay every minimum, pay the extra on the debt first in the order of your method, then type each payment in Debt payments with its minimum, extra, interest and balance after.
Month-close routine, in this order: update each balance in Debts, add the month to Net worth, read Minimums against pay, read the Extra payment plan and run the Avalanche Order Check.
Run Snowball Against Avalanche when you choose a method and the Extra Payment Test when you can pay more; every date and saving is an estimate from your numbers, never a promise.
Debt ratios compare with typical ranges you can edit in Settings: a typical range, check your own numbers. They are not advice and not a lending decision.
A single adult with one income and no children can use every sheet: type your own debts, leave Partner 2 and the joint account empty, and use Partner 1 as the owner.
Use the 18 tools for the big questions, print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details written in.
Read the dashboard and the Charts page each month: total debt, interest, extra payments and the debt-free dates.

Why a workbook: one flat price, no yearly renewal, your data stays with you and there is nothing to link or re-connect; you type or paste your own data. It works in Excel and Google Sheets with no macros.
What this is not: it is not a bank app, and not tax, legal, investment or credit advice; check your local rules and ask your adviser. Every verdict is an estimate from your numbers.

listing.title: Debt Payoff Planner Excel Template: Snowball vs Avalanche, Extra Payment Calculator, Debt Free Date, Minimum Payments, Debt Ratios
listing.headline: Pay off cards and loans: snowball or avalanche, with your own numbers
listing.description:
Plan how your household pays off cards and loans in one Excel workbook, for a single adult, a couple or a family. Type your debts with balance, yearly rate, minimum payment and due day, and the workbook builds the snowball order (smallest balance first) and the avalanche order (highest rate first), with a 60-month schedule for each, the debt-free date and the total interest. When a debt is cleared, its payment rolls to the next one.

Snowball Against Avalanche shows both orders side by side. The Extra Payment Test shows what each step of extra payment saves in months and interest against paying only the minimums, and the Extra Payment Solver finds the extra a month that clears every debt by the date you want. The Avalanche Order Check finds the debt with the highest rate and the interest lost each year if the extra payment goes elsewhere. Windfall to Debt applies a bonus or refund to the highest rate first.

The Minimum Payments Check compares your minimums with take-home pay and with a limit you set, and tests what happens if income falls. Debt Ratios compares your debt payments with typical ranges that you edit in Settings: a typical range, check your own numbers, never advice. A Due Days Map shows which due dates fall just before payday and suggests a day to ask your lender for. Balance history, interest paid by month and payments by debt show the year.

18 decision tools, 12 printable sheets, 12 documents, 12 checklists and 34 ready text messages come with it. This is part four of the Household Finance suite. A standard .xlsx workbook that works in Excel and Google Sheets, with no macros, no subscription and no bank links: you type or paste your own data. The demo copy is full of sample data. All dates and savings are estimates from your numbers, never promises. It is a household money kit, not a bank app, and not tax, legal, investment or credit advice.

competitors.lacks: has a debt screen but no snowball against avalanche on your own numbers, no extra payment solver and a yearly or monthly fee, and bank links break
orders by balance only: no avalanche comparison, no windfall test, no due days against payday and no ratios against typical ranges
stops at one payoff date: no minimum payments check, no interest lost by the current split and no history of balances and interest
handles one loan at a time: no rolling payments from a cleared debt to the next, no schedule for all debts together
